extraction.name: ScienceQA
extraction.description: ScienceQA is a large-scale multimodal multiple choice dataset containing 21,208 science questions collected from elementary and high school science curricula, covering natural science, social science, and language science. Each example includes a question, multiple choices, multimodal contexts, a correct answer, a lecture, and an explanation to support chain-of-thought reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sourced from IXL Learning, an online K-12 education platform. Original science problems were downloaded and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, solutions) were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, and semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid questions (those with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates) were manually removed. If multiple correct answers applied, only one correct answer was kept.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems from IXL Learning, an online K-12 education platform aligned with California Common Core Content Standards, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers answered test questions and evaluated model-generated explanations. For human performance study: 4,241 test questions split into 425 batches of 10, with 5 training questions as exam examples per batch; workers needed to correctly answer 4/5 exam questions to qualify. For explanation evaluation: workers rated explanations on relevance, correctness, and completeness; batches of 10 assigned to 3 workers each; majority vote used for final scores.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority vote used to determine human scores for each explanation. Blind studies conducted to verify dataset robustness, showing results close to random chance for Q only and CI only conditions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 workers per batch for both human performance study and explanation evaluation
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: VIT-GPT2 image captioning model used to generate captions for images in the dataset
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing datasets fail to provide annotations for the answers, or are restricted to the textual-only modality, small scales, and limited domain diversity. ScienceQA addresses these but is collected from elementary and high school science curricula, which may limit generalization beyond that scope.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve AI interpretability and multi-hop reasoning in science education contexts, potentially benefiting educational AI systems that can explain their reasoning to students.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, validation, and testing of multimodal multiple-choice science question answering models, as well as for benchmarking multi-hop reasoning ability and interpretability of AI systems. It supports few-shot learning and fine-tuning of large language models.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Questions without any context have their context text replaced with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For human performance study, test questions were shuffled and split into batches of 10, with randomly added training questions as exam examples. Workers who failed to correctly answer 4 out of 5 exam examples were eliminated. For GPT-3 experiments, in-context examples were selected using random seeds across four trials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For language models, newline separators (\n) in text are replaced with \\n when encoding inputs. Image captions are generated using a captioning model (vit-gpt2-image-captioning) with maximum caption length of 16, 4 beams, and maximum 512 output tokens. VQA baselines use a maximum of 100 input words or tokens.
